title: Create a scratch project document, write into it, route later runs at it by document_id, and close it
task: Build something in a fresh scratch project instead of the user's model: Connector.CreateProjectDocument creates a headless document (no window, active:false, UIDocument null), Connector.WithTransaction writes into it in the same run, list_instances gives its document_id for later runs, and closing it needs Connector.Settle then Document.Close from a run routed elsewhere with confirm_lifecycle_actions.

pitfalls.symptom: Document.Close on the scratch document throws InvalidOperationException when the run is routed at that document (document_id points at it).
pitfalls.cause: The routed document has the run's transaction group open; a document cannot close itself from inside its own run.
pitfalls.fix: Route the closing run at another document (omit document_id), find the scratch document by Title in Application.Documents, Settle it, then Close. The failure is per call, not permanent.

pitfalls.symptom: `script-lifecycle-confirmation-required`: the script is refused before it runs because it calls Close/Save/SaveAs.
pitfalls.cause: Lifecycle calls act outside the transaction that rolls a failed script back.
pitfalls.fix: Pass confirm_lifecycle_actions: true to execute_script after the user agrees.

pitfalls.symptom: Close/SaveAs refused with a transaction or group still open on the document.
pitfalls.cause: Revit refuses lifecycle calls while any transaction or group is open; the run's group is open on every document it wrote to.
pitfalls.fix: Connector.Settle(doc, keep: true|false) first; a document-settled-kept/discarded notice reports it.

pitfalls.symptom: UIDocument is null; UIDocument.ActiveView throws NullReferenceException.
pitfalls.cause: A created (or background) document has no window.
pitfalls.fix: Use Document and collectors; do UI work (RequestViewChange) routed at the active document.

pitfalls.symptom: Documents pile up in the session after several runs.
pitfalls.cause: Created documents stay open until closed; a throw before cleanup leaves them open (their writes are rolled back, their existence is not).
pitfalls.fix: Return each created document's title, close in the same run when the work is done, or on the next run by title with confirm_lifecycle_actions: true.

pitfalls.symptom: After doc.Close() every member of that Document throws 'The referenced object is not valid, possibly because it has been deleted from the database'.
pitfalls.cause: Close disposes the document; the managed wrapper outlives it but nothing behind it does.
pitfalls.fix: Copy Title, PathName and any ids you still need into locals before Close, and verify closure by the remembered title.
